articles.title: U.S. midterm elections impact on India: faster trade deal talks and higher tariffs likely
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The results of the U.S. midterm elections, which show that the Democrats have gained control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, will likely speed up talks between India and the U.S. on a trade deal but could also see higher tariffs on India until the deal is closed, according to experts.

On the one hand, a desire to now quickly close the trade deal to show strength domestically could induce Mr. Trump to increase his tariff pressure on India, while on the other, Indian negotiators will likely see this election result as an opportunity to push through a favourable deal for India.
U.S. midterm elections: Follow LIVE updates from the results on November 4, 2026

According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of the trade think-tank Global Trade Research Initiative, this loss will push U.S. President Donald Trump to increase his exercise of his executive powers to pressure India into accepting a deal.
“With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win,” Mr. Srivastava said. “Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout.”

Leaders in the U.S. and India have repeatedly said over the last few months that the deal between the two countries is nearly ready and is awaiting final approvals. India, in particular, has been holding out until it receives an assurance that it will win a clear advantage over its competitors.

“Trump will now use his executive powers to pressure India for a quick deal that secures market access for U.S. agricultural and industrial goods, alongside other major concessions for U.S. companies,” Mr. Srivastava said.

While the U.S. Supreme Court in February defanged Mr. Trump’s reciprocal tariff policy that had seen tariffs of up to 50% being levied on India, the President has other tools through which he can levy tariffs.

According to Deep Pal, Director of Geopolitics and Policy at the Koan Advisory Group, the implications of these election results might lead to some difficulty for Mr. Trump in gaining support for his policies.

“For this administration, especially after tonight, any decision has to look like a win domestically, to core Republican voters,” Mr. Pal said. “With Congress out of his hands, a lot will depend on how much control Mr. Trump has over the Republican party and if there will be any purchase for his ideas.”
However, Mr. Pal pointed out that the Indian government might view this new reality in the U.S. with greater optimism.

“Indian negotiators, on the other hand, may think that the new realities will make the Trump administration amenable to a better trade deal for India, breaking the current deadlock, and leading to a flurry of new conversations,” Mr. Pal said.

articles.title: SC stays Madras HC order on Chidambaram temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) questioned whether State High Courts have parens patriae (guardian) jurisdiction only over public temples and not places of worship of other faiths while staying a Madras High Court order that constituted a Board of Management to administer the ancient Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple in Tamil Nadu back to glory.

A Bench of Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi issued notice to the State of Tamil Nadu and froze the implementation of the October 30 High Court order, which said the Podhu Dikshidar (a hereditary community of priests) had maladministered the temple ever since its running was handed over to them following orders passed by the Supreme Court in 2014.

The High Court had appointed retired judges V. Bharathidasan and R. Suresh Kumar to chair the Board of Management (BoM). Retired IAS officer C. Rajendran was designated its member, and the secretary of the Podhu Dikshidar’s association and the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department secretary would be the ex-officio members.

The BoM, in consultation with the Tamil Nadu Heritage Commission, was ordered to undertake the removal of unauthorised constructions put up on the temple premises that caused damage to the ancient structure. The High Court Bench had tasked the BoM to take steps to retrieve the temple properties under encroachment with the help of the district administration.

Appearing for Tamil Nadu government, senior advocates Shekhar Naphade and Jaideep Gupta submitted that there was severe damage caused to the property and the Podhu Dikshidars had not shared the full accounts of the income derived from the temple in the last 12 years.
Mr. Naphade said the High Court had parens patriae jurisdiction over public temples to protect the interest of the presiding deity, considered as juristic person by law.
“Is this parens patriae only for temples or other places of worship?” Justice Kumar asked the State government.
Mr. Naphade responded that the law only recognised parens patriae jurisdiction for public temples, not churches or other places of worship of faiths.
Senior advocate Sai Deepak Iyer, for the opposite side, submitted that the court should look into why parens patriae doctrine applied to temples alone.
“Please, do not make any sweeping statements,” Justice Kumar said.
Mr. Gupta said the primary question was whether the temple was in danger or not. Mr. Naphade said, “This is a prime instance of what maladministration would happen on returning a temple”.

articles.title: Why even a strong El Niño does not guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the summer of 1997, one of the strongest El Niños of the 20th century took shape in the Pacific Ocean. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicted a monsoon rainfall deficit of 8% below the average, as was expected in El Niño years. However, by the end of September that year, rainfall levels were nearly normal.

This year, a “ferocious” El Niño is taking shape, and is expected to peak only in December. The 2026 southwest monsoon ended nearly 13% below the long-term average of 87 cm. East and Northeast India had their driest season since records began in 1901.

articles.title: With no illegal immigrants found on draft electoral rolls, SIR greatly inconvenienced people: Owaisi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hyderabad parliamentarian Asaduddin Owaisi on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) said the claim of illegal immigrants being included in electoral rolls had caused considerable hardship, particularly to the poor, who lost at least two days’ wages completing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, even as officials said there was no evidence of illegal migrants being included in the draft electoral rolls.

Referring to the statement made by Hyderabad District Election Officer R.V. Karnan, that no foreign nationals or illegal migrants were found in the draft electoral rolls after the revision exercise, Mr. Owaisi said the finding had exposed the claims repeatedly made by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Sangh parivar leaders as false. He said that thousands of people were put through the verification process and daily wage earners were forced to forego income to furnish documents and complete enrolment formalities.

Touching upon the issue of Qadeemi Masjid located within the Krishi Bhavan complex in New Delhi , Mr. Owaisi criticised the Union government’s attempts to remove the structure as part of the Common Central Secretariat redevelopment under the Central Vista project. Earlier in the day, he had posted on X that the Centre had informed the Delhi High Court that the masjid was “impermissible and incompatible with the secular character of government property” and therefore needed to be removed.

Mr. Owaisi, who is the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president, noted that the Central Vista project itself was inaugurated with a Bhoomi Pooja (ground breaking ceremony) and remarked that “secularism is not offended by the use of one faith’s rituals for a public project, but is allergic to a masjid that has stood there even before 1912”. He said the masjid predated Krishi Bhavan and even the development of Lutyens’ Delhi.

The AIMIM chief said the masjid was part of the country’s cultural heritage and had not been included in the land acquisition process undertaken by the British for the development of New Delhi. He sought Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju’s intervention and said the government should recognise the historical and legal status of the mosque. He added that any dispute over the property could be adjudicated before the Waqf Tribunal. “The mosque was there before Delhi became the national capital. What exactly do they want to do with it now?” he asked.

Mr. Owaisi also criticised what he described as attempts to diminish the political aspirations of Muslims. Recalling remarks often made by BJP leaders about “Abdul” being confined to repairing punctures, he said Muslims would no longer be intimidated by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and would emerge as political leaders.

articles.title: Bus fare hike avoidable had Karnataka government cleared its own dues: BJP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Taking serious exception to the hike in bus fare of Karnataka’s State-run RTCs , the Opposition BJP has argued that there was no need for a hike if the government had cleared its own dues to the tune of ₹5,650.95 crore towards transport corporations.
Addressing a press conference, Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok alleged that “the government has acted wrongly by choosing to shift the burden on people instead of clearing the outstanding amount.”

He announced that the BJP will hold a statewide protest on November 5 against the bus fare hike. Intense protests will be held in all district headquarters and in Bengaluru, Mr. Ashok said. He described the hike as arbitrary while stating that it has touched a high of 40% in some cases.
“The Congress government has raised bus fares in a manner which is more disgraceful than the Tughlaq regime. No previous government has ever increased fares to this extent,” he remarked.
“Even though Deepavali is a festival of lights, this year it has turned out to be a festival of darkness due to the hike,” he alleged.

articles.title: Cabinet clears ₹14,500 crore viability gap funding scheme for 92 GWh battery energy storage systems
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) approved ₹14,500 crore in viability gap funding for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage systems between FY27 and FY31.
This development is significant given India's ambitious target of 500 GW of renewable energy by 2030.

The scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh storage capacity across three technologies — Battery Energy Storage System (30 GWh), Pumped Storage Projects (60 GWh) and Emerging Storage Technologies (2GW), Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said in a media briefing in New Delhi.
The Minister said the scheme will be implemented for five years till 2030-31.

articles.title: Union Cabinet approves ₹14,500 crore VGF scheme to develop large scale energy storage in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet has approved a ₹14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for the development of grid-scale energy storage systems for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31, the government announced on Wednesday.
According to the government, the scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh of fresh, yet-to-be-commissioned, energy storage capacity across the country.

“The scheme will support creation of new capacities equivalent to 170% of the present-day grid scale energy storage system capacity in the country and help meet the required grid scale ESS capacity of 411 GWh by 2031-32,” the government said in a release.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Can battery storage save India’s renewable energy grid? | Business Matters

The scheme is designed to provide for the development of 60 GWh of hydro pumped storage plant (PSP) capacity, 30 GWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity and 2 GWh of capacity through alternative energy storage technologies, with a total estimated investment of ₹97,600 crore.

“The VGF support will help improve the financial viability of these projects and accelerate the deployment of large-scale energy storage infrastructure in the country,” the government said, adding that the scheme will also provide an impetus to domestic manufacturing of battery energy storage systems.

As per the government’s release, energy storage capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process with both public and private sector electricity distribution companies eligible for VGF support for BESS and hydro PSP projects.
Projects based on alternative energy storage technologies, too, will be implemented by public and private sector entities.

“To promote indigenous manufacturing, BESS projects will be subject to a minimum Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) of 40%,” the government added. “The requirement will encourage domestic manufacturing, create opportunities for Indian industry and complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing.”

articles.title: Supreme Court upholds States’ power to levy additional sales tax, says case has become academic
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) held that a 1974 Constitution Bench ruling upholding States’ power to impose additional sales tax or surcharge calculated as a percentage of the existing sales tax continues to hold the field, saying a reference on the issue had become academic.

A seven-judge Constitution Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant unanimously held that the legal question referred to it nearly 27 years ago no longer required adjudication, as the statutory provisions under challenge had since been replaced or amended and the Goods and Services Tax (GST) law had come into force.

“The question referred to is of no practical significance and now academic. Consequently, the question referred to does not survive for adjudication by a seven-judge Bench, and the reference has to be answered accordingly,” the CJI, who wrote the judgment on behalf of himself and five other judges, said.
The Bench also comprised Justices K.V. Viswanathan, S.V.N. Bhatti, Joymalya Bagchi, N.V. Anjaria, Arun Palli and V. Mohana.
Justice Viswanathan wrote a separate concurring verdict.

While declining to undertake a fresh adjudication on the reference, the Court clarified that the five-judge Constitution Bench ruling in S. Kodar vs State of Kerala (1974) continued to hold the field.
The earlier judgment had upheld additional sales tax, rejecting the argument that such a levy amounted to a tax on the income of dealers.

“We have clarified that the case clearly held that an additional tax or surcharge computed as a percentage of the sales tax payable is an enhancement of the rate of sales tax and a tax on the sale or purchase of goods within Entry 54 of List II, as it then stood. That decision continues to hold the field,” the CJI said.
The Court further held that the question of the legislative competence of State legislatures to impose the surcharge would be governed by the law laid down in S. Kodar.

The reference arose from a challenge to Section 5A of the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947, which provided for additional tax at the rate of 10% on dealers with an annual turnover between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore, and 15% on dealers whose turnover exceeded ₹1 crore.

The appellants questioned whether the State legislature was competent to impose such a levy under Entry 54 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, which empowered States to tax the sale or purchase of goods, or whether it effectively amounted to a tax on income, a subject falling within Parliament’s domain under Entry 82 of List I.

The controversy stemmed from differing interpretations in earlier Supreme Court decisions. In S. Kodar vs State of Kerala, a five-judge Bench had upheld additional sales tax, ruling that a levy calculated with reference to the sales tax payable was an enhancement of the sales tax rate and not a tax on the dealer’s income.

articles.title: Services sector activity hits 4-month high in October as business conditions improve cautiously
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India's services sector activity recorded the strongest pace of expansion in four months in October as demand buoyancy fuelled growth in business activity and new orders amid easing cost pressures, a monthly survey said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Companies were cautiously optimistic about the outlook, and they lifted jobs to the least extent in four months. The latest expansion in international sales was the weakest in almost four years.
The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Services PMI Business Activity Index rose from 55.2 in September to 55.8 in October, indicating the strongest pace of growth for four months.
In the Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) parlance, a print above 50 means expansion, while a score below 50 denotes contraction.

"India's services PMI rose to 55.8 in October, a four-month high, as business conditions improved cautiously. Although overall demand remained fairly strong, new export orders recorded the slowest pace of expansion since February 2023," Pranjul Bhandari, Chief India Economist at HSBC, said.

Survey participants identified new business growth as the main driver behind the rise in output, the survey said, adding that favourable demand conditions, new client wins and successful advertising boosted new order intakes.

On the prices front, there was a substantial decline in cost pressures. "Input and output prices continued to rise, but at a slower pace than in the previous month, signalling some relief from inflation pressures," Bhandari said.
Employment growth also slowed to its weakest pace since June, suggesting that some service sector businesses have sufficient capacity to meet current staffing requirements, she said.
Companies were, however, cautiously optimistic about the outlook, and they lifted jobs to the least extent in four months.
Meanwhile, India's composite PMI increased to 56.2 in October, from 55.9 in September, marking the fastest rise in aggregate output in four months and reflecting healthy business activity.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections impact on India: faster trade deal talks and higher tariffs likely
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The results of the U.S. midterm elections, which show that the Democrats have gained control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, will likely speed up talks between India and the U.S. on a trade deal but could also see higher tariffs on India until the deal is closed, according to experts.

On the one hand, a desire to now quickly close the trade deal to show strength domestically could induce Mr. Trump to increase his tariff pressure on India, while on the other, Indian negotiators will likely see this election result as an opportunity to push through a favourable deal for India.
U.S. midterm elections: Follow LIVE updates from the results on November 4, 2026

According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of the trade think-tank Global Trade Research Initiative, this loss will push U.S. President Donald Trump to increase his exercise of his executive powers to pressure India into accepting a deal.
“With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win,” Mr. Srivastava said. “Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout.”

Leaders in the U.S. and India have repeatedly said over the last few months that the deal between the two countries is nearly ready and is awaiting final approvals. India, in particular, has been holding out until it receives an assurance that it will win a clear advantage over its competitors.

“Trump will now use his executive powers to pressure India for a quick deal that secures market access for U.S. agricultural and industrial goods, alongside other major concessions for U.S. companies,” Mr. Srivastava said.

While the U.S. Supreme Court in February defanged Mr. Trump’s reciprocal tariff policy that had seen tariffs of up to 50% being levied on India, the President has other tools through which he can levy tariffs.

According to Deep Pal, Director of Geopolitics and Policy at the Koan Advisory Group, the implications of these election results might lead to some difficulty for Mr. Trump in gaining support for his policies.

“For this administration, especially after tonight, any decision has to look like a win domestically, to core Republican voters,” Mr. Pal said. “With Congress out of his hands, a lot will depend on how much control Mr. Trump has over the Republican party and if there will be any purchase for his ideas.”
However, Mr. Pal pointed out that the Indian government might view this new reality in the U.S. with greater optimism.

“Indian negotiators, on the other hand, may think that the new realities will make the Trump administration amenable to a better trade deal for India, breaking the current deadlock, and leading to a flurry of new conversations,” Mr. Pal said.

The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Although the memo did not specify the contours of the scheme and its ambit, the policy has been in the works for some time now.
The Hindu had learnt previously that the potential scheme could provide support of about 30% for setting up of these processing plants.

At an event of the industry body FIMI in September this year, Secretary at the Union Ministry of Mines Keshav Chandra had indicated that the government would institute a scheme for domestic processing of lithium and nickel.

Back in April, the Piyush Goyal, the former secretary, had indicated that the government had identified two minerals for initiating the scheme that were, among other things, expected to provide resilience the electric vehicle battery chain.

Grid-scale energy storage systems are deployed at transmission and distribution for greater grid stability, absorb excess electricity when supply exceeds demand and discharge them during peak hours or when necessary.

About 1,835 million units (MUs) of renewable energy was curtailed, according to data compiled by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) during July and August this year. This includes 1,462 MU of solar energy and 373 MU of wind energy.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries is already implementing a production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for establishing 50 GWh of advanced chemistry cell manufacturing capacity, of which 10 GWh would account for grid-scale stationary storage.

fullParagraphs: Oil prices rose on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) in a volatile session as investors ​awaited Washington’s next move in the war with Iran, with ⁠Democrats capturing control of US Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republicans in midterm elections.
Brent futures rose 82 cents, or 0.8%, to $104.42 a barrel at 0510 GMT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude ‌futures gained 50 cents, or 0.5%, to $96.59, reversing earlier declines.
In the previous session, Brent settled at its lowest level in nearly four weeks ‌as traders weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
Vote ‌counting ⁠was underway in the U.S. midterm elections, with Democrats snaring majorities ⁠in both houses of Congress for the rest of Trump’s second term.

“President Trump’s conflicting signals, with military strikes continuing alongside statements downplaying further escalation, have made it difficult for traders to build strong directional ​conviction,” said Priyanka Sachdeva, head ‌of market insights at Phillip Nova.
“I believe some profit-taking and reduction in speculative long positions are justified, particularly after the sharp rally in October,” said Sachdeva.

“However, the underlying supply disruption risks around the Strait of Hormuz have not disappeared. ‌An unexpected drawdown in U.S. crude inventories is also offering some fundamental ​support,” she added.

The U.S. had carried out “defensive” strikes on Iran’s Qeshm island targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said ⁠on Tuesday. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.
Markets remained on watch for any progress in talks ‌to end the US-Israeli war with Iran, as Qatar stepped up mediation efforts to avert an escalation of attacks after the US elections.
A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran and the United States remain far from a deal to end their war.
U.S. President Donald Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that the United States had no immediate plans to strike Iran.

articles.title: China must make extradition request if it wants two Uyghur men returned: Thailand
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Thailand said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that China must make a formal extradition request if it wants two Uyghur men returned, in response to growing concerns and fears of abuse or torture if they are returned. The two men, in letters shared last week, pleaded not to be sent back to China.

Thailand’s head of the National Security Council Chaipruak Doungprapat said his agency will not make a decision on their deportation, unlike the case of 40 Uyghur men who were sent back to China last year . He said the process will go through the courts and the men will be able to defend themselves. If the court rules in their favour, it’s possible for them to be sent to another country for resettlement.
“But if the court rules against them, they will be extradited according to the treaty. This is the judicial process,” he said.

Human rights activists and some Thai politicians have raised concerns in recent days that the two men, who have been held in Thailand for more than a decade, will be sent back to China imminently. The two men were released from prison in late October and are currently held at the Suan Plu immigration detention centre in Bangkok.

China has consistently pushed for the return of a group of 300 Uyghurs who were detained by Thai authorities in 2014 when they were on their way to the Thai-Malaysia border, saying they were terrorists.

China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Mao Ning on Wednesday said “China and Thailand’s cooperation in combating cross-border crimes, including illegal immigration, is in accordance with the laws of both countries, as well as international law and international practice.” Ms. Mao didn't comment on whether China had sent an extradition request.

The two men, a 26-year-old and a 35-year-old, wrote letters that were then shared publicly last week. “Every time we are worrying from China to take back us,” one of them wrote in a letter shared by Kannavee Suebsang, a former lawmaker and founder of the Peace Rights Foundation, a human rights group that represents the men. “We aren’t terrorist," the Uyghur man wrote.

Sasinan Thamnithinan, a lawmaker from the Opposition People's Party, said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that Thailand is obligated by both domestic and international law to ensure that no individual is returned to a country where they could face torture or inhumane treatment.

“Maintaining international relations is important, but it must not take precedence over human rights and the rule of law. No one should be sent back to face danger simply because the government wants to end a problem,” Ms. Sasinan said in a statement.

Uyghurs are a Turkic, majority Muslim ethnic group native to Xinjiang in China's northwest. After decades of conflict with Beijing over discrimination and suppression of their cultural identity, the Chinese government launched a brutal crackdown on the Uyghurs that some Western governments have called a genocide.

The two men were part of a group of more than 300 Uyghurs fleeing China that were detained in 2014 by Thai authorities near the Malaysian border. Of this group, Thailand sent a group of mostly women and children to Turkey. Then in 2015, Thailand deported 109 of those still detained to China against their will, prompting an international outcry which saw the Thai embassy in Turkiye ransacked in protest. For more than a decade, the Thai government put off a decision on what to do about the group.
In February 2025, Thailand sent back 40 Uyghur men to China, despite pleas from Thai lawmakers and UN officials not to deport them.

fullParagraphs: Several Indian-origin candidates too notched up victories as Democrats made significant gains in the US midterm elections on November 3, 2026, positioning themselves to wrest key Senate seats from Republicans, delivering a stinging rebuke to President Donald Trump.

Indian-American candidates Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives from Virginia and Florida, respectively. On the other hand, Republican ‌Vivek ‌Ramaswamy ‌was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor.

Suhas Subramanyam, who served as an advisor to former president Barack Obama, has been re-elected as a member of the US House of Representatives. The 40-year-old won from Virginia’s 10th congressional district , polling over 61.5% of the vote against Republican Dave Beckwith, who managed to win 36.4 per cent of the ballots cast.

Ro Khanna has won re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, located in the heart of Silicon Valley. The 50-year-old is completing his fifth term and will begin his sixth in January. Khanna was born in Philadelphia to a middle-class family. Both his parents immigrated to the United States from India in the 1970s.

Pramila Jayapal, who represents Washington’s 7th Congressional District, has secured a sixth term in the House of Representatives. Last month, her criticism of India’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls drew a public rebuke from India’s ambassador to the US. Jayapal, who was first elected to Congress in 2016, has been a prominent voice on immigration reform and healthcare issues.

A former high school principal, Pia Dandiya became the newest Indian-American to be elected to the US House , defeating Republican Casey Askar in Florida’s 22nd Congressional district. Dandiya bagged 51.9% of the votes, while her opponent Askar polled 49.1% of the votes.

Indian-American Democratic lawmaker Ami Bera has won the re-election to the U.S. House in California’s 3rd Congressional District, defeating Republican Robb Tucker. The 61-year-old won his eighth term in the US House of Representatives. Physician-turned-politician Amerish Babulal ‘Ami’ Bera is the longest-serving Indian American in the US Congress and is considered a strong voice on healthcare and diplomacy, as per PTI.

Born in Andhra Pradesh, Miller immigrated to the United States with her family at the age of seven. Miller represented District 15 in the Maryland House of Delegates from 2010 to 2018.

Other Indian-American candidates are awaiting their results as vote counting is still under way. articles.title: Israel election commission rejects Benjamin Netanyahu charges of fraud
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Israeli electoral authorities on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) rejected allegations promoted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fraud by Arab parties, who could hold the key to removing him from power after a divisive vote.

President Isaac Herzog will at noon (10:00 GMT) officially receive the results of the October 27 election as he decides whether to give Mr. Netanyahu or his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, the first chance to form a government, with neither commanding enough votes alone.
The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and was confident that the announced results "accurately reflect the will of the voters".
"All complaints submitted by political factions have been reviewed and there were no findings indicating harm to the integrity of the election," it said in a statement.

Mr. Netanyahu has repeatedly alleged fraud by Arab-majority parties, pointing to the arrests of several people with envelopes of cash on election day and later saying lawmakers received money from Qatar -- allegations that have been levelled at his own aides in the past.

Late on Tuesday (November 3), Israeli Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara said she would not question anyone without evidence after reports that the head of the domestic security service Shin Bet, a Netanyahu ally, had asked to interrogate Arab parties.
Mr. Netanyahu's Likud party lashed out at her, saying that she was trying to "obstruct the investigation and to cover up this serious case of manipulation of the electoral process by foreign actors".

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief trying to unite centrists and the centre-right and turn the page on Mr. Netanyahu's long, polarising reign, accused Likud of attempting a "pogrom against democracy".

He had earlier warned Mr. Netanyahu against launching a new war with his close ally U.S. President Donald Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli Prime Minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.
Yair Lapid, a former Prime Minister and key force in the opposition bloc, pointed to the midterm elections in the United States in which Democrats resoundingly trounced Trump's Republicans.
The Shin Bet "outbursts" paired with the U.S. election results "eliminate any possibility of a unity government led by Netanyahu".
Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister who has been in power on and off for nearly two decades, has called for a "broad national government" -- with himself at the top.

fullParagraphs: Indian-origin candidates are seeking office across the United States in the November 3, 2026, midterm elections, the polls are so called because they fall midway through a President’s four-year term

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are due for election, since members serve two-year terms. In the Senate, where members serve six years, 35 of the 100 seats are up for election, including special elections in Ohio and Florida.

The Indian-origin candidates are contesting from States including California, Washington, Virginia, Arizona, Florida, Texas, Ohio, New York and Maryland. Their races span different levels of government, from the U.S. Congress and State executive offices to city leadership positions.

Several Indian-Americans are in the fray across Texas, Florida, Arizona, Ohio, New York and Los Angeles. Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress.
Here are some of the prominent Indian-origin candidates contesting the midterm elections:

Congressman Ro Khanna is a member of the progressive wing of the Democratic Party. His grandfather, Amarnath Vidyalankar, was a freedom fighter who was imprisoned alongside Mahatma Gandhi and later served as a Congress Member of Parliament.

Mr. Khanna is a second-generation immigrant. His father, a chemical engineer from the Indian Institute of Technology, and his mother, a school teacher, migrated to the United States from Punjab. Born in Philadelphia, Mr. Khanna studied economics at the University of Chicago before earning a law degree from Yale Law School. He later worked as an intellectual property lawyer with clients from the technology sector.

A Democrat from California, Mr. Khanna is seeking re-election from California’s 17th Congressional District, which includes parts of Silicon Valley. He has criticised President Donald Trump’s policies as “utterly destructive”, described him as a “lame duck”, and said Democrats would prevail in the 2026 midterm elections and the 2028 presidential election.

Congresswoman Jayapal, who was born in Chennai, is seeking another term from Washington’s 7th Congressional District. In 2020, she became the second Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives.
Ms. Jayapal traces her roots to Kerala. Her mother, Maya Jayapal, is a writer and counsellor and the author of Bangalore: Roots and Beyond .
Ms. Jayapal was the first Indian-American woman elected to the U.S. House of Representatives and has represented Washington’s 7th Congressional District since 2017.

On October 14, 2026, Ms. Jayapal voiced concern over reports about the removal of 13 crore names from draft electoral rolls in India. The Democratic lawmaker said she supported non-violent protests against what she described as anti-democratic efforts.

articles.title: Attack on vessel near Hormuz Strait: Deceased sailor hailed from Gujarat, kin plan burial in Oman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A 25-year-old sailor who died after a suspected drone attack on an Indian-flagged cargo vessel off the Oman coast near the Strait of Hormuz hailed from Gujarat’s Devbhumi Dwarka district, a relative of the vessel owner said on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Nahim Ajij Gandhar was among the 14 crew members on board the vessel, which was registered at Bedi port in Gujarat’s Jamnagar district. He said all the crew members were residents of Salaya.
The sailor’s family has decided to conduct Gandhar’s burial in Oman, citing delays in completing formalities, he said.

The projectile hit, which triggered strong condemnation from India, destroyed the mechanised sailing vessel (MSV) and the consignment of dates it was carrying, said Akbar Ahmed Sumbhaniya, whose younger brother Jusab owns the vessel.

An MSV is a hybrid watercraft that retains traditional sailing rigs and hull designs (such as wooden cargo dhows or kotias) while also being fitted with a mechanical propulsion engine (typically a diesel engine) and a propeller.

The vessel, Al Jusufi, was carrying nearly 900 metric tonnes of dates from Hamriyah port in the United Arab Emirates to Porbandar when it was struck on November 2 off the Oman coast near Limah, said Mr. Sumbhaniya.

“Gandhar was at the steering wheel inside the cabin when the attack took place. One side of his leg was completely fractured, and his left hand was also badly injured,” Mr. Sumbhaniya told PTI over the phone from Salaya.

Mr. Sumbhaniya said he received a call from the MSV’s captain at around 4.45 p.m. on November 2, informing him that the vessel had come under a drone attack and caught fire. “Within five minutes of the attack, the crew members boarded a lifeboat,” he said.

The vessel was sailing close to the Omani coastline, around 2 km from the shore and a few nautical miles after crossing the port of Limah, when the suspected drone attack took place, according to Mr. Sumbhaniya.
He said the attack destroyed the vessel, causing a loss of ₹2-3 crore, and the consignment of dates.
Mr. Sumbhaniya said the MSV operated from Salaya, where he and his brother live.
The crew had been deployed on the vessel three to four months ago after travelling from Gujarat to the UAE in May-June, he said.

articles.title: Why psoriasis can sometimes be hard to diagnose and when you need to see a doctor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Psoriasis is an autoimmune condition that causes thick, scaly patches on the skin. However, it often remains unidentified and undiagnosed because it does not look the same on all parts of the body: it could be mistaken, for instance, for dandruff on the scalp, persistent eczema on the palms, or a fungal infection. You can’t always judge psoriasis by looking only at visible parts of the skin.

Why does this happen? Our skin isn’t the same everywhere. The thickness of the skin can vary considerably depending on the diversity of the environmental conditions that it is exposed to and the kind of treatment given to it. These factors can contribute to how psoriasis appears and feels.

articles.title: Hackers target France’s blood bank freezers, reprogram storage to 110°C
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: A major cyberattack targeted cold storage facilities of France’s national blood agency , Etablissement Francais du Sang (EFS), after hackers breached systems to remotely heat freezers holding donor blood samples and plasma.
The incident was reported between November 1 and 2, when unknown bad actors compromised Coolworld, a key refrigeration maintenance contractor for EFS.
They reprogrammed cold storage units, typically kept at a freezing −30°C to safely preserve blood products, by pushing temperature settings up to 110°C (230°F).

However, an on-duty technician noticed this abnormal overnight temperature spike on monitoring systems, and averted the damage. Rapid emergency protocols allowed technical teams to intervene before permanent damage affected the inventory.
France’s Ministry of Health confirmed that the breach was contained with zero operational disruption to hospital supplies or transfusion services.

While the EFS initially reported that the impacted containers held routine health-monitoring blood samples, official statements later confirmed that frozen plasma meant for medical transfusions was also stored within the affected refrigeration units.
The incident coincided with a broader wave of cyber intrusions targeting networked industrial cooling systems, including supermarket refrigeration across roughly a dozen European nations.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Green hydrogen is a form of renewable energy that, if taken up widely, could reduce global greenhouse gas emissions. It is produced by splitting water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen using renewable power. This clean, zero-emissions fuel is mainly used by industries like steel manufacturing and chemical refining. Heavy transport sectors such as maritime shipping, aviation and long-haul trucking could also use it.

But green hydrogen comes at an environmental cost too: huge amounts of water are needed to produce it. In Africa, the regions that have the best solar and wind resources to produce this clean energy are also those with the least water on the planet.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu takes baby steps towards conservation of Bengal fox, golden jackal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu government is taking baby steps towards conservation of Bengal foxes and golden jackals which are critical to ensure the ecological balance of the habitats.

In his March 2025 Budget speech, the then Forests Minister K. Ponmudy had announced in the State Legislative Assembly of a conservation plan for the Bengal fox and jackal, which are critical to maintain the ecological balance of the habitats.

Tamil Nadu, renowned for its exceptional biodiversity, has diverse ecosystems — from coastal plains to mountainous terrains. Among the many species that inhabit these landscapes are the Indian Bengal fox (Vulpes bengalensis) and the golden jackal (Canis aureus), both of which play vital roles in maintaining ecological balance as predators and scavengers.

Both species are presently listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, affording them the highest level of legal protection in India. The level of their decline in the recent past was made out from the fact that the Indian Bengal fox and the golden jackal were both listed in Schedule V (Vermin category) when the Wildlife (Protection) Act was enacted in 1972.

Advanced Institute for Wildlife Conservation (AIWC) had conducted a preliminary study to identify their presence in landscapes across Tamil Nadu and found that their numbers and ranges had dwindled over the past three to four decades. The survey indicated that they had disappeared in many districts and were found only in pockets in the districts of Dharmapuri, Tiruvannamalai, Salem, Villupuram and Madurai.

The government then decided that immediate conservation interventions were necessary keeping in mind their ecological importance and growing threats faced by them. The Chief Wildlife Warden had sent a proposal to the government for funding for comprehensive assessment of current threats, habitat use, and distribution patterns to develop an effective, long-term conservation roadmap.

The objectives were identification of critical habitats in and outside Protected Areas (PA)and Reserved Forests, habitat protection and improvement measures and control of poaching, creation of awareness on the need to conserve these species amongst the various stakeholders and an establishment of a captive breeding centre in Salem Zoo.

The erstwhile DMK government accorded administrative and financial sanction for ₹2 crore but it required the approval of the Legislature by inclusion in the revised Supplementary Estimates for the year 2025-26. Now, the Chief Wildlife Warden has sent a proposal for ₹92.5 lakh and use the unspent balance from the last fiscal. The State government, after careful consideration, agreed to the proposal and sanctioned ₹1.3 crore this year.

However, forest officials said the conservation plan would require an inter-departmental coordination as these two are considered edge-species, living between the forests and the agricultural landscapes.

articles.title: Business, unusual: On engaging with the Myanmar junta
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist.

The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. It has also played both sides, dealing with the junta and powerful rebel groups such as the Kachin Independence Organisation, whose territory is rich in rare earths and jade, and the United Wa State Army, which runs a massive tin mine. New Delhi wants to revive its stalled Act East policy, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project. The U.S. eyes access to mining vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium, for use in electric vehicles and weapons systems. What these short-sighted overtures miss is that trade thrives in a country at peace, not one where armed groups are perennially battling for control. The junta which has killed its citizens and has scuttled every move towards democracy cannot deliver that peace. Unless the generals are made to answer for their war crimes, Myanmar will remain a war zone. It will be ruinous not only for its hapless people but also for businesses seeking to trade with it.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: United stand: On protests against SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

articles.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 28, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: U.S. midterm elections impact on India: faster trade deal talks and higher tariffs likely
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The results of the U.S. midterm elections, which show that the Democrats have gained control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives, will likely speed up talks between India and the U.S. on a trade deal but could also see higher tariffs on India until the deal is closed, according to experts.

On the one hand, a desire to now quickly close the trade deal to show strength domestically could induce Mr. Trump to increase his tariff pressure on India, while on the other, Indian negotiators will likely see this election result as an opportunity to push through a favourable deal for India.
U.S. midterm elections: Follow LIVE updates from the results on November 4, 2026

According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of the trade think-tank Global Trade Research Initiative, this loss will push U.S. President Donald Trump to increase his exercise of his executive powers to pressure India into accepting a deal.
“With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win,” Mr. Srivastava said. “Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout.”

Leaders in the U.S. and India have repeatedly said over the last few months that the deal between the two countries is nearly ready and is awaiting final approvals. India, in particular, has been holding out until it receives an assurance that it will win a clear advantage over its competitors.

“Trump will now use his executive powers to pressure India for a quick deal that secures market access for U.S. agricultural and industrial goods, alongside other major concessions for U.S. companies,” Mr. Srivastava said.

While the U.S. Supreme Court in February defanged Mr. Trump’s reciprocal tariff policy that had seen tariffs of up to 50% being levied on India, the President has other tools through which he can levy tariffs.

According to Deep Pal, Director of Geopolitics and Policy at the Koan Advisory Group, the implications of these election results might lead to some difficulty for Mr. Trump in gaining support for his policies.

“For this administration, especially after tonight, any decision has to look like a win domestically, to core Republican voters,” Mr. Pal said. “With Congress out of his hands, a lot will depend on how much control Mr. Trump has over the Republican party and if there will be any purchase for his ideas.”
However, Mr. Pal pointed out that the Indian government might view this new reality in the U.S. with greater optimism.

“Indian negotiators, on the other hand, may think that the new realities will make the Trump administration amenable to a better trade deal for India, breaking the current deadlock, and leading to a flurry of new conversations,” Mr. Pal said.

articles.title: SC stays Madras HC order on Chidambaram temple
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) questioned whether State High Courts have parens patriae (guardian) jurisdiction only over public temples and not places of worship of other faiths while staying a Madras High Court order that constituted a Board of Management to administer the ancient Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple in Tamil Nadu back to glory.

A Bench of Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi issued notice to the State of Tamil Nadu and froze the implementation of the October 30 High Court order, which said the Podhu Dikshidar (a hereditary community of priests) had maladministered the temple ever since its running was handed over to them following orders passed by the Supreme Court in 2014.

The High Court had appointed retired judges V. Bharathidasan and R. Suresh Kumar to chair the Board of Management (BoM). Retired IAS officer C. Rajendran was designated its member, and the secretary of the Podhu Dikshidar’s association and the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department secretary would be the ex-officio members.

The BoM, in consultation with the Tamil Nadu Heritage Commission, was ordered to undertake the removal of unauthorised constructions put up on the temple premises that caused damage to the ancient structure. The High Court Bench had tasked the BoM to take steps to retrieve the temple properties under encroachment with the help of the district administration.

Appearing for Tamil Nadu government, senior advocates Shekhar Naphade and Jaideep Gupta submitted that there was severe damage caused to the property and the Podhu Dikshidars had not shared the full accounts of the income derived from the temple in the last 12 years.
Mr. Naphade said the High Court had parens patriae jurisdiction over public temples to protect the interest of the presiding deity, considered as juristic person by law.
“Is this parens patriae only for temples or other places of worship?” Justice Kumar asked the State government.
Mr. Naphade responded that the law only recognised parens patriae jurisdiction for public temples, not churches or other places of worship of faiths.
Senior advocate Sai Deepak Iyer, for the opposite side, submitted that the court should look into why parens patriae doctrine applied to temples alone.
“Please, do not make any sweeping statements,” Justice Kumar said.
Mr. Gupta said the primary question was whether the temple was in danger or not. Mr. Naphade said, “This is a prime instance of what maladministration would happen on returning a temple”.

articles.title: Why even a strong El Niño does not guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the summer of 1997, one of the strongest El Niños of the 20th century took shape in the Pacific Ocean. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicted a monsoon rainfall deficit of 8% below the average, as was expected in El Niño years. However, by the end of September that year, rainfall levels were nearly normal.

This year, a “ferocious” El Niño is taking shape, and is expected to peak only in December. The 2026 southwest monsoon ended nearly 13% below the long-term average of 87 cm. East and Northeast India had their driest season since records began in 1901.

articles.title: With no illegal immigrants found on draft electoral rolls, SIR greatly inconvenienced people: Owaisi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hyderabad parliamentarian Asaduddin Owaisi on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) said the claim of illegal immigrants being included in electoral rolls had caused considerable hardship, particularly to the poor, who lost at least two days’ wages completing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, even as officials said there was no evidence of illegal migrants being included in the draft electoral rolls.

Referring to the statement made by Hyderabad District Election Officer R.V. Karnan, that no foreign nationals or illegal migrants were found in the draft electoral rolls after the revision exercise, Mr. Owaisi said the finding had exposed the claims repeatedly made by Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Sangh parivar leaders as false. He said that thousands of people were put through the verification process and daily wage earners were forced to forego income to furnish documents and complete enrolment formalities.

Touching upon the issue of Qadeemi Masjid located within the Krishi Bhavan complex in New Delhi , Mr. Owaisi criticised the Union government’s attempts to remove the structure as part of the Common Central Secretariat redevelopment under the Central Vista project. Earlier in the day, he had posted on X that the Centre had informed the Delhi High Court that the masjid was “impermissible and incompatible with the secular character of government property” and therefore needed to be removed.

Mr. Owaisi, who is the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president, noted that the Central Vista project itself was inaugurated with a Bhoomi Pooja (ground breaking ceremony) and remarked that “secularism is not offended by the use of one faith’s rituals for a public project, but is allergic to a masjid that has stood there even before 1912”. He said the masjid predated Krishi Bhavan and even the development of Lutyens’ Delhi.

The AIMIM chief said the masjid was part of the country’s cultural heritage and had not been included in the land acquisition process undertaken by the British for the development of New Delhi. He sought Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju’s intervention and said the government should recognise the historical and legal status of the mosque. He added that any dispute over the property could be adjudicated before the Waqf Tribunal. “The mosque was there before Delhi became the national capital. What exactly do they want to do with it now?” he asked.

Mr. Owaisi also criticised what he described as attempts to diminish the political aspirations of Muslims. Recalling remarks often made by BJP leaders about “Abdul” being confined to repairing punctures, he said Muslims would no longer be intimidated by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and would emerge as political leaders.

articles.title: Union Cabinet approves ₹14,500 crore VGF scheme to develop large scale energy storage in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Union Cabinet has approved a ₹14,500 crore Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for the development of grid-scale energy storage systems for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31, the government announced on Wednesday.
According to the government, the scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh of fresh, yet-to-be-commissioned, energy storage capacity across the country.

“The scheme will support creation of new capacities equivalent to 170% of the present-day grid scale energy storage system capacity in the country and help meet the required grid scale ESS capacity of 411 GWh by 2031-32,” the government said in a release.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Can battery storage save India’s renewable energy grid? | Business Matters

The scheme is designed to provide for the development of 60 GWh of hydro pumped storage plant (PSP) capacity, 30 GWh of battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity and 2 GWh of capacity through alternative energy storage technologies, with a total estimated investment of ₹97,600 crore.

“The VGF support will help improve the financial viability of these projects and accelerate the deployment of large-scale energy storage infrastructure in the country,” the government said, adding that the scheme will also provide an impetus to domestic manufacturing of battery energy storage systems.

As per the government’s release, energy storage capacity will be allocated through a tariff-based competitive bidding process with both public and private sector electricity distribution companies eligible for VGF support for BESS and hydro PSP projects.
Projects based on alternative energy storage technologies, too, will be implemented by public and private sector entities.

“To promote indigenous manufacturing, BESS projects will be subject to a minimum Domestic Content Requirement (DCR) of 40%,” the government added. “The requirement will encourage domestic manufacturing, create opportunities for Indian industry and complement existing supply-side incentives for battery manufacturing.”

articles.title: Supreme Court upholds States’ power to levy additional sales tax, says case has become academic
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) held that a 1974 Constitution Bench ruling upholding States’ power to impose additional sales tax or surcharge calculated as a percentage of the existing sales tax continues to hold the field, saying a reference on the issue had become academic.

A seven-judge Constitution Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant unanimously held that the legal question referred to it nearly 27 years ago no longer required adjudication, as the statutory provisions under challenge had since been replaced or amended and the Goods and Services Tax (GST) law had come into force.

“The question referred to is of no practical significance and now academic. Consequently, the question referred to does not survive for adjudication by a seven-judge Bench, and the reference has to be answered accordingly,” the CJI, who wrote the judgment on behalf of himself and five other judges, said.
The Bench also comprised Justices K.V. Viswanathan, S.V.N. Bhatti, Joymalya Bagchi, N.V. Anjaria, Arun Palli and V. Mohana.
Justice Viswanathan wrote a separate concurring verdict.

While declining to undertake a fresh adjudication on the reference, the Court clarified that the five-judge Constitution Bench ruling in S. Kodar vs State of Kerala (1974) continued to hold the field.
The earlier judgment had upheld additional sales tax, rejecting the argument that such a levy amounted to a tax on the income of dealers.

“We have clarified that the case clearly held that an additional tax or surcharge computed as a percentage of the sales tax payable is an enhancement of the rate of sales tax and a tax on the sale or purchase of goods within Entry 54 of List II, as it then stood. That decision continues to hold the field,” the CJI said.
The Court further held that the question of the legislative competence of State legislatures to impose the surcharge would be governed by the law laid down in S. Kodar.

The reference arose from a challenge to Section 5A of the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947, which provided for additional tax at the rate of 10% on dealers with an annual turnover between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore, and 15% on dealers whose turnover exceeded ₹1 crore.

The appellants questioned whether the State legislature was competent to impose such a levy under Entry 54 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, which empowered States to tax the sale or purchase of goods, or whether it effectively amounted to a tax on income, a subject falling within Parliament’s domain under Entry 82 of List I.

The controversy stemmed from differing interpretations in earlier Supreme Court decisions. In S. Kodar vs State of Kerala, a five-judge Bench had upheld additional sales tax, ruling that a levy calculated with reference to the sales tax payable was an enhancement of the sales tax rate and not a tax on the dealer’s income.
